decisions.reason: The spec describes a 2D game with simple graphics, movement, and UI elements (health bars), which are all well-suited for implementation using Pygame. There are no complex physics or scene management requirements that would necessitate Godot.
The spec does not specify a resolution, so a standard 800x600 resolution is chosen as a sensible default for a simple 2D game.
The spec does not specify an FPS, so 60 FPS is chosen as a standard smooth frame rate for real-time games.
The spec does not specify movement speed. A moderate speed is chosen to allow responsive player control.

decisions.choice: A jump velocity that results in a moderate jump height.
decisions.reason: The spec does not specify jump height. A moderate jump height is chosen to allow for tactical movement without being excessive.
The spec states 'a short fixed distance' for opponent pushback. 20 pixels is chosen as a noticeable but not overly disruptive distance.
The spec states 'flash white briefly'. 10 frames is chosen as a visually clear but brief duration.
The spec states 'punches when close'. 50 pixels is chosen as a reasonable 'close' distance for the AI to initiate a punch.
The spec mentions a 'plain wooden-brown floor' but not its size or position. It's assumed to be a strip at the bottom of the screen.
The spec asks for a 'light background colour'. Light grey is a neutral and common choice.
The spec asks for a 'plain wooden-brown floor'. This RGB value represents a typical wooden brown.
